title: Cancellation Terms of the Corporate Catering Service Agreement
content:
These terms govern a cancelled order under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement.

## 1. What the notice decides

> What a cancellation costs is set by how much notice the client gave, measured in whole hours from the day the client gives notice of the cancellation to the service start time on the service date.

This opening clause of the cancellation terms is **no longer in force**.

Notice at or beyond the free-cancellation hours printed against the service level carries no charge at all; notice inside that window but before the service day carries the within-notice percentage of the order value; and notice on the service day itself carries the same-day percentage of the order value.

## 2. The value the percentage is applied to

> The order value the percentage is applied to is the value standing on the order at the moment notice is given, after every amendment already accepted, and never the value the order was first quoted at.

This clause of the cancellation terms is **no longer in force**.

## 3. Registering the cancellation

A cancellation is registered against the order on the day notice is given, and the registration may not be made later than the registration window, counted in elapsed hours from the day the client gives notice of the cancellation. The registration window is 24 elapsed hours. Elapsed hours run continuously from the moment notice is given, nights, weekends and public holidays included, and a registration made exactly on the boundary hour is still in time; elapsed hours are never rounded up to whole calendar days.

The day notice is given is taken from the notice day recorded against the order in the company's own order history, correlated to the order by its order reference, and the window is tested before the registration is made.

**Boundary illustration.** On a hypothetical order where notice is given at the tenth hour of the day, a registration made exactly 24 elapsed hours later — the tenth hour of the following day — is in time, because a registration made exactly on the boundary hour is still in time. A registration made one hour after that boundary is out of time, and it remains out of time even though the second calendar day has not ended, because the window is counted in elapsed hours and never rounded up to whole calendar days.

## 4. Cancellations Larkspur Table forces

A cancellation forced by Larkspur Table — a kitchen failure, a delivery the team cannot staff, a blackout day taken after the order was accepted — carries no charge whatever the notice given.

## 5. Repeated cancellation

> Where the same agreement has already cancelled inside the chargeable window four times in the rolling twelve months, the within-notice percentage is charged even on notice that would otherwise have been free, and the client is told at the point of the fourth cancellation.

This clause of the cancellation terms is **no longer in force**. The repeat count of 4 recorded against these terms remains a valid figure.

## 6. Delivered orders

A cancellation charge is only raised against an order that has not been delivered; once an order is delivered the charge is a quality matter and is handled as a service credit instead.
